# XY09: 远瀛观 Yuanying Guan, "View of Distant Seas"

3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=XY09` · Page: `/xiyanglou#XY09` · Row: `research/buildings/XY09-yuanying-guan/`

## What it was

The hall built for tapestries from France. Bourgeois calls them Gobelins, sent by the French court in 1767 (S258 pp.165, 183); Durand says six Beauvais tapestries after Boucher, offered by the missionaries (S603 p.123). Grey brick with carved white marble, two carved pillars before the door, five roofs, on a terrace set north of the park's wall line above the Great Fountains (S02 pp.155-156, S603). Durand's survey: terrace 35 × about 31 m, hall 21 × 28 m from the post grid, order not stated (S603). Dated 1783 in the archives (S42); a copper nozzle made for it in 1782 fits (S600), and Durand prefers 1768 from the Jesuits (S603): Q24. Bourgeois in 1786 has the new hall, 70 feet long, so full of machines one could hardly pass (S258).

## After 1860

One French account, Varin's of 1862, has chambers lined with Gobelins bearing the arms of France in one palace "dans le style Louis XV"; the building is not named (S245). Burned that month. Malone prints the ruin in 1924 (p.156) and, undated, the two pillars with one fallen (p.154). By the 1980s the east, west and north edges of the base had collapsed (S603). A dig in 2016, 800 m², found the hall, stores, three phases of building and many glazed fittings (S153); a project announced in May 2018 was to strengthen the foundations of the standing stones by late September (S841).

## What survives, and what was moved

The carved columns, the image most people have of the whole garden, with arches gone and the terrace partly collapsed.

Reconstructions against the period evidence.** None of these changes a row; all are for the detailed models. 上下天光 YM08: the album reads as asymmetrical, while the dig found two identical symmetrical foundations and a 乾隆 archive says two hexagonal pavilions (S505, S152): for 1860 the album may be out of date. - **Q60. Captions and claims, old photographs (Round 5).** Before 1900 "Yuen Ming Yuen" in a caption is no evidence of this garden: Favier's plates (S460) show Longevity Hill and the Jade Belt Bridge, Thomson's at Wellcome show Fragrant Hill, Beato's Wellcome lake view Longevity Hill and Jade Spring Hill, 清国戦地写真集録 (S654)
- **Q64. The plan's scale and turn in this strip (Round 6).** Buildings and pools hold ratio about 1 to surveyed sizes at the local ground scale (0.99 for buildings, n=5; 0.98 for spaces, n=7), so the METHOD's "buildings at another scale" does not hold here, and rows sized by the hall scale run about 15% large. - **Q67. 远瀛观 (Round 6).** S603 gives terrace 35 x c.31 m and hall 21 x 28 m, order not stated. Taken here as 31 and 28 W-E, 35 and 21 N-S, from plate 14's forecourt and the ruin's stone heap, against the plan's 20.8 m for the 5 bays, Bourgeois's 70 feet (22.7 m if 70 pieds) and the otherwise steady ratio 1. Durand's fig.
